newsitem.title: USA: Sudbury, Intermet up on merger news.
newsitem.headline: Sudbury, Intermet up on merger news.

text.p: Shares in Sudbury Inc rose 2-1/8 to 12-1/8 on Tuesday after news that the Cleveland-based automotive and industrial supplier agreed to be acquired by Intermet Corp for 12-1/2 a share in cash.
Intermet, a ferrous casting foundry company, was up 1 to 13-1/4. Detroit-based Intermet is also an automotive supplier.

The companies announced late on Monday a definitive merger agreement under which Intermet will promptly begin a cash tender offer for all of Sudbury's 15.6 million outstanding shares (diluted, with 4.2 million represented by stock options and participation certificates).

"It looks like a clear-cut deal" that has the blessing of Sudbury management," Jerry Dombcik, director of research at McDonald & Co, said. "It doesn't preclude somebody coming in with a higher offer, but I don't think it's likely."
He said the Sudbury price rise was due to the news.
Mark Brody, Sudbury's chief financial officer, said tender offer documents to be sent out within five days will outline when the offer will commence and other details.
